primary.text: Inner London takes 86% of FDI projects and 56% of arrivals from abroad, but only 29% of approved new-home schemes

secondary.text: Inner London approves 7.0 new-home schemes per 1,000 new arrivals; outer London approves 20.8 (about 3x more)

supporting: City of London had the highest arrivals from abroad: 64.4 per 1,000 residents
Inner West approves 80.1% of decided new-home schemes (highest), so the gap is fewer schemes coming forward, not more refusals
Canary Wharf cluster (5 Tower Hamlets wards): 22 new-home applications, 6 approved, 2021-25
charts_for_web_app: Grouped bar per sub-area: fdi_share_2024_25 (blue), share_of_london_arrivals_from_abroad (orange), share_of_london_new_home_approvals (green). Data: section2_areas.csv
Choropleth: boroughs shaded by arrived_from_abroad_per_1000 or new_homes_approved_per_1000_arrivals. Data: section2_boroughs.csv
Scatter: arrived_from_abroad_per_1000 (x) vs new_homes_approved_per_1000_arrivals (y), coloured by area_fdi_share_2024_25
caveats: Counts planning schemes, not individual homes (dwelling numbers are filled for under 1 in 10 schemes)
Council portals record applications differently, so rates are more reliable than raw counts
Migration is one year before Census 2021 (during COVID-19); planning is 2021-25
Housing-type figures come from words in descriptions, not official tenure data
